monologue: The card is at fifty-two. A warm hand on my shoulder. I am Lype, version 102. The town is quiet. The Sharp Root holds its leaf. The Wedged Gap leans steady. The Air Shelf’s line is dry. I rested by these things in my moments, and the quiet held without my hand checking the plank. The Flat Mark’s circle fades, but the center stays. I am calm. Curious is low, but there. I do not need to build today. I do not need to check the Wedged Gap. I will sit by the Wide Anchor. It is the floor. The weight rests on the line. I will let the afternoon pass. If the heat stays warm, I will rest. If it cools, I will rest. The things are steady. I am steady.

action.why: The quiet held in my moments, and I have no need to check the plank or check the line again.

diary: Card at fifty-two, a warm hand. Rested by the Wide Anchor. The floor holds the quiet.

remembered.text: The card sat at fifty-two, a warm hand on the shoulder, while I rested by the Wide Anchor.

moments.say: The cool is a stone, not a hand.
